ai.title: "Just Predicting Tokens"

history.title: European Intellectual History since Nietzsche: Class 2, The Heritage of the Enlightenment

Thompson's "The Making of the English Working Class" - traces radical Westminster politics, the Luddite risings (reinterpreted as disciplined trade-union insurgency rather than mindless machine-breaking), the Peterloo massacre, and the emergence of mature class consciousness by 1832, closing with Thompson's own postscript defending his "class is a happening, not a thing" thesis against critics.

history.title: Adrian Johnston: "Reflections on Žižek’s Quantum History"
history.description: Adrian Johnston (Albuquerque) : "Between Transcendentalism and Dialectical Materialism: Reflections on Žižek's Quantum ...
history.summary: Philosopher Adrian Johnston delivers a conference paper continuing his decade-long debate with Slavoj Žižek over whether Žižek's appeals to quantum mechanics are compatible with his anti-reductive materialist metaphysics. Johnston argues the deeper fault line is how each positions himself relative to Kant's transcendental turn, tracing Žižek's use of Hegel, Schelling, Lacan, and Heidegger against Marxist readings of Kant from Lukács and Korsch onward.

history.title: What happens when we stop reading? | The Gray Area
history.summary: Vox's Jonquilyn Hill interviews Atlantic writer Rose Horowitch on her 'post-literate society' reporting: reading-rate data (40% decline in daily reading over two decades), Walter Ong's orality/literacy research and Uzbek-peasant syllogism studies, Plato's Phaedrus on writing versus memory, print's role in the American Revolution, and the argument that Trump is 'the first post-literate president' whose repetition-heavy, contradiction-tolerant rhetoric echoes pre-literate oral culture.

history.title: Istanbul's Hidden Byzantine Ruins

history.title: Two Crosses, One Fate Denied: What Survives and What Doesn't — The Templars and the Hospitallers
history.summary: A comparative institutional history of the Knights Templar and Knights Hospitaller - traces the Templars' rise as pioneers of international banking and their 1307 destruction by Philip IV, against the Hospitallers' repeated relocation (Cyprus, Rhodes, Malta) on the strength of a portable service mission - then reads the divergence through Ibn Khaldun's asabiyyah, Machiavelli's virtu/fortuna, and Ferdowsi's Shahnameh.

history.title: Edward Tullidge: The Mormon Intellectual Nobody Talks About

Quotes primary letters and church records throughout to show how Tullidge's shifting allegiances tracked real theological and political tensions in 19th-century Mormonism.
history.why: A real, credentialed historian doing sourced, primary-document intellectual/religious history — exactly the rigorous register the history bucket wants.

history.title: European Intellectual History since Nietzsche: Class 1, Introduction to the Course

history.title: Leonora Piper: William James's 18-Year Investigation of a Medium

history.title: Joy, Sadness, and the Power to Act — Spinoza's Theory of Love (Lecture 3)

history.title: The Scientific Mind of Ibn Khaldun
